note: Every place Sega's manual and the cartridge library disagree, and every place this package reads something the manual does not settle. Each entry names what the document says, what the cartridges do, which one this package follows, and what evidence would close the question.
authority: hardware.json holds the ladder. Rung 1 is Sega's reference manual, rung 2 is a cartridge, rung 3 is nothing. The manual is an instruction to a licensee rather than a description of silicon, and a retyped one, so a genuine cartridge that disagrees with it is a fact about cartridges rather than an error.

divergences.topic: Which bytes the stored checksum is taken over.

documentSays.claim: Every byte of the ROM is summed except the two that hold the checksum.
documentSays.quote: A 16-bit checksum for the ROM (low-hi order). $7FFA and $7FFB are not included in this checksum.
documentSays.source: Software Reference Manual for the SEGA Mark III Console, page 22

thisPackageDid.claim: Sums every byte up to the declared size except the whole sixteen-byte header.
thisPackageDid.why: Leaving out only the two checksum bytes reproduces the stored value on no image at all, so the sentence cannot describe what licensees' tools actually wrote.

measured.note: Distinct images that carry a header and declare a size this reading knows, walked by conformance/census.py over the Master System and Game Gear libraries.
measured.measuredBy: python3 -m conformance.divergences <library> for the document rule; the package rule is the corpus figure

divergences.wouldCloseIt: A rule that reproduces the stored checksum on the retail images the package rule misses, read from the export boot program that checks it rather than inferred from the images.

divergences.topic: How long the string that opens the header is.

documentSays.claim: Ten bytes: TMR SEGA followed by two spaces.
documentSays.source: Software Reference Manual for the SEGA Mark III Console, page 22

thisPackageDid.claim: Looks for the first eight bytes, TMR SEGA, and nothing after them.
thisPackageDid.why: Most headers in the library carry other bytes where the two spaces would be, so requiring them would refuse genuine cartridges.

measured.note: Distinct images with the eight-byte string at one of the three candidate addresses.

divergences.wouldReopenIt: A boot program that compares all ten bytes and refuses a cartridge without the two spaces.

documentSays.claim: Every size code printed carries a high nibble of 4.
documentSays.source: Software Reference Manual for the SEGA Mark III Console, page 22

thisPackageDid.claim: Reads 3 as a Japanese Master System and 5, 6 and 7 as the three Game Gear regions.
thisPackageDid.why: These are the codes the library carries, and the Game Gear ones are on Game Gear cartridges only.

measured.smsJapan: 31 images, 12 of them reproducing their checksum
measured.ggExport: 335 images, 3 of them reproducing their checksum
measured.ggInternational: 431 images, 11 of them reproducing their checksum

divergences.wouldCloseIt: A Sega document for the Game Gear or for the Japanese Master System that prints the region codes.

documentSays.source: Software Reference Manual for the SEGA Mark III Console, page 22

thisPackageDid.claim: Reads a low nibble of 1 as 512K and 2 as 1M.
thisPackageDid.why: Images that large exist, and reading the codes that way makes most of them reproduce their checksum.

measured.declared512K: 17 images, 13 of them reproducing their checksum
measured.declared1M: 2 images, 1 of them reproducing its checksum

divergences.wouldCloseIt: A Sega document printing the codes, or a boot program that decodes them.
